title: Lord! Subdue Our Selfish Will
description: Lord! Subdue Our Selfish Will in Tonic Solfa to HEINLEIN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 505, “Brotherly Love”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to HEINLEIN; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord! sub-due our self-ish will; Each to each our tem-pers suit, By Thy mod-u-lat-ing skill, Heart to heart, as lute to lute.

lines: Each to each our tempers suit,
Heart to heart, as lute to lute.
Music for the King of kings!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to HEINLEIN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
